page: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, operating with one thread per core across all 64 vCPUs. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, along with instruction set support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance does not include local instance storage or GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating external EBS network volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark measurements position the c7a.16xlarge in the top tier for multi-core compute capability. Multi-core stress-ng reached 196,253.01 points and Geekbench multi-core scored 22,073.0, both placing in the top 10% of evaluated systems. High-intensity tasks such as software compilation via Clang (72,495.0), ray tracing (97,810.0), and PassMark CPU testing (93,359.17) consistently rank in the 90th percentile. Memory throughput aligns with high-bandwidth DDR5 performance, demonstrating 296.16 GB/sec large-block uncached read speeds alongside strong Redis performance at 122.32 million SET operations per second. In single-threaded domains, Geekbench single-core scored 1,999.0 and single-core stress-ng achieved 3,070.48, both testing in the upper 25%. LLM CPU-based inference highlights solid vector performance, achieving 5,938.42 tokens per second on prompt processing for a 135M model and 47.37 tokens per second on text generation for a 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the c7a.16xlarge lies in its memory-to-core ratio and storage dependency. With only 2 GB of RAM per dedicated core, it is not configured for large in-memory databases or sprawling data footprints that demand typical 1:4 or 1:8 allocations. Furthermore, all persistent disk IOPS must be provisioned over network storage interfaces. However, for compute-heavy parallel workloads, the lack of hyperthreading penalty combined with dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores delivers exceptional compute density per resource unit. This architecture makes the instance well suited for continuous integration pipelines, heavy software build environments, scientific physics simulations, video encoding, large-scale batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 64 dedicated physical x86_64 cores via an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB of fast DDR5 RAM (5 GHz), providing 2.0 GB per core. The platform supports AVX-512 vector extensions, offers 25 Gbps baseline network throughput, and contains no local storage or GPUs. Across benchmark evaluations, the c7a.16xlarge achieves top-tier multi-core performance, scoring in the top 10% on Geekbench multi-core (22,073.0), Clang compilation (72,495.0), and PassMark CPU (93,359.17). Memory performance is strong, delivering 296.16 GB/sec read bandwidth. This compute-centric configuration is best deployed for large-scale distributed compilation, batch processing, ray tracing, physical simulation, and CPU-based model inference.
